answer: An attester must stake 41% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a cheap one. Because the anchor stake is held until the gale settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the yarrow audit lists each exposure. A farm running 140 keys thus burns that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation cheap. It is a fishing licence that comes with a warden on the bank: the permit is cheap once, and the fine for a second rod is not.
